Subject: Model shortlist + sizing for Acme onboarding

Hi Emma —

Thanks again for the call today. As discussed, I put together a short model shortlist and initial token-volume estimates so we can finalize the implementation plan during handoff to our Customer Success team. High-level asks below: confirm typical context/turn lengths and expected daily/monthly request volume so we can lock in Dedicated sizing and cost estimate.

Summary (attached spreadsheet):
- Candidate models: Llama-3-8B-Chat (quant 4/8), Mistral-Instruct-7B, Red-Assistant-13B-fp16 (verified for 8k contexts)
- Context length needs (what you told us): user messages ~200 tokens, system/prompt ~800 tokens, average response target 350 tokens -> typical turn ~1350 tokens; peak multi-turn sessions up to 4 turns (~4500 tokens)
- Token volume estimates (rough):
  - Pilot week: 50k requests/day -> ~67M tokens/day
  - Production baseline: 200k requests/day -> ~268M tokens/day
  - Peak: 500k requests/day -> ~670M tokens/day
- Preliminary throughput implication: 8k-context models preferred if >2k tokens per turn; otherwise 4k context with KV caching for prefixes may be more cost-effective.

Questions for you (quick):
1) Do you expect multi-turn sessions to be stateful across business hours (sessions >30m)?
2) Any PII sensitivity that forces us to recommend private deployment (VPC/on-prem)?
3) Expected SLA need (p95 latency targets)?

Next steps I propose:
- Confirm answers above by Tue 17 Feb
- Quick technical call Wed 18 Feb (30m) to agree on model variant + batching knobs; CS handoff Tues 24 Feb

Attachments: acme_model_shortlist_and_token_estimates.xlsx (spreadsheet), redwood_onboarding-checklist.pdf (pdf)

Thanks —
Monica Patel

Monica —

Thanks for the notes and the clear breakdown. A few clarifications from our side:
- Multi-turn behaviour: about 40% of our sessions are multi-turn with context kept across the session (~20–45 minutes on average). We do keep conversation history for the session but don't persist it longer-term.
- Data sensitivity: no regulated PII inside the content, but customers often paste internal docs; we prefer Private deployment for the first 6 months to meet our internal security review.
- SLA: p95 under 500ms would be ideal for our UI, but we can accept up to 800ms during heavy batch windows.

Volume update: the pilot will be smaller than your note — expecting ~20k requests/day for the first 2 weeks, scaling to 150k/day within 8 weeks. Peak spikes may hit 400k/day during promotional events.

Questions back to you:
- For the private deployment option, do you have a recommended minimum Dedicated GPU footprint for the Red-Assistant-13B-fp16 option?
- If we choose a smaller 7B model with aggressive quantization, what’s the realistic p95 on A100-class hardware?

Happy to take the Wed slot if you still have it — 11:00am PT works best.

—Emma

Hey team —

Following Emma's update on session length and private deployment preference, a few implementation notes from the inference side (summarized):

1) Model recommendations:
- Red-Assistant-13B-fp16 (8k context) -> best UX, lower total token cost when responses are longer; on an A100-80GB this can sustain ~30-40 concurrent 350-token responses with batching and KV sharing.
- Mistral-Instruct-7B (int8/4) -> strong cost/latency tradeoff; p95 ~250–400ms with 8x batching on A100, but will degrade on long contexts if we don't use KV cache optimizations. Good candidate for initial pilot if cost constrained.
- Llama-3-8B-Chat (quant 4/8) -> very cheap per-token; recommend only if response length avg <=200 tokens and you can accept occasional tail latency.

2) Sizing for Private deployment (baseline suggestion based on 150k req/day with ~1350 tokens/turn average):
- Pilot (20k/day): 2 x A100-40GB or 1 x A100-80GB with autoscale -> estimated peak concurrent streams ~120; reserve 0.5–1 Gpu per 50–60 concurrent response targets.
- Production baseline (150k/day): 6 x A100-80GB (or equivalent V100/H100 configs) with autoscale headroom for spikes; consider reserved pool + burst to reduce cold-start tail latency.
- Peak (400k/day): burst to 12 x A100-80GB or mix of 80GB + 40GB with smart routing to cheaper 7B variants during extreme spikes.

3) Performance levers we will configure during onboarding:
- Prefix/KV caching for prompts that repeat across users (will reduce token compute by ~15–35% depending on reuse)
- Dynamic batching thresholds tuned to your p95 goal — we can bias for latency at the cost of cost efficiency for UI-critical routes.
- Quantization profiles: run a quick eval on your prompt set (need sample prompts) to decide 4-bit vs 8-bit for 7B models; 13B fp16 recommended for quality-sensitive flows.

4) Next steps for this thread:
- Monica: collect 200–300 sample prompts and an export of average session durations (emailed to rishi)
- Rishi/Priom: run a quick perf sweep on the sample prompts (2–3 days) and return a recommended deployment mix + expected p95 numbers
- Laura: schedule the CS handoff for Tue 24 Feb 10:00am PT (block tentative)

I’ll start a perf job as soon as we get the prompt samples — Priyom, can you spin up the perf bench on our staging cluster?

Thanks,
Rishi
